[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L5 adds gut-wall efflux and intestinal-metabolism experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for presystemic loss, with direction and experimental context preserved; mechanism alone is not a direct oral-bioavailability result.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Cladribine, the closest 2-halogenated deoxyadenosine analog, had absolute oral bioavailability of 36-46% in fasted patients (C10, C15, C24); L5 shows it is a BCRP substrate (C155, C159, C176, C190, C151, C153), yet its measured F remains well above 20%, so gut-wall efflux in this class does not imply F < 20%.
Didanosine, a polar purine nucleoside with low PAMPA permeability and probenecid-sensitive secretory transport, had fasted F of 22-28% (C03, C13, C121, C165), still above the threshold.

EFdA, the closest 2-fluoroadenine nucleoside in L5, showed measurable Caco-2 A-to-B permeability of about 4.8-6.0 x 10^-7 cm/s with pH-independent transport (C193, C196), providing no affirmative efflux or intestinal-metabolism barrier for the 2-fluoroadenine core.

Other polar nucleosides (lamivudine, emtricitabine, zalcitabine) had fasted F of 69-95%, 92%, and 30-80%, respectively (C01, C04, C26, C25, C41), supporting that low passive permeability does not translate to F < 20%.

L5 records show nucleoside transporters (ENT1/2, CNT3) mediate intestinal uptake of nucleoside analogs including cladribine, ribavirin, NHC, and GS-441524 (C177, C181, C187, C154, C163, C164), providing a plausible absorptive route for the query despite low passive permeability.
The high efflux ratio reported for GS-441524 (C172) is structurally distant (pyrrolotriazine C-nucleoside) and lacks an F value; it is not affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability or IV-comparator exposure measurement exists for the query molecule.
No direct gut-wall efflux or intestinal metabolism measurement exists for the query; L5 records are for analogs (EFdA, cladribine, didanosine, GS-441524).
The query's pyranose sugar differs from the furanose/oxathiolane sugars of the supporting analogs, limiting structural transferability.
No human PK data exist for the query; some supporting F values are from mice or different patient populations.
GS-441524's high efflux ratio is structurally distant and lacks an F value, so it cannot serve as affirmative low evidence.
content.decision_summary: Prediction remains high (F >= 20%): direct F values for close nucleoside analogs (cladribine 36-46%, didanosine 22-28%, lamivudine 69-95%, emtricitabine 92%, zalcitabine 30-80%) all exceed the threshold. L5 gut-wall efflux/intestinal metabolism evidence shows BCRP efflux in cladribine and secretory transport in didanosine without reducing F below 20%, and the closest 2-fluoroadenine analog EFdA shows measurable pH-independent Caco-2 permeability; no affirmative threshold-relevant low evidence was added. Confidence remains moderate due to lack of direct query measurements and the sugar-ring difference.

messages.content:
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L5 adds gut-wall efflux and intestinal-metabolism experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for presystemic loss, with direction and experimental context preserved; mechanism alone is not a direct oral-bioavailability result.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

L3, L4, and L5 append one ranked Stage 3 record bundle each; all earlier cards remain visible.","record_sampling":"Each context and level shows a deterministic sample of at most ten raw records. available_record_counts reports the full pool before sampling. That does not make them negative, invalid, or independent votes; use them only as additional experimental context.
